svg.data-vd-play-label: Play: the origin of bread wheat
svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "Bread wheat evolved by hybridisation and polyploidy."], [1, "Two wild diploid grasses, AA and BB (2n = 14 each), crossed."], [3.5, "Their hybrid AB was sterile: the chromosomes had no partners in meiosis."], [5.5, "The chromosome number doubled: AABB, emmer wheat, tetraploid and fertile (2n = 28)."], [8.5, "Emmer crossed with another goat grass, DD."], [11, "The sterile ABD hybrid doubled to AABBDD: bread wheat, hexaploid, 2n = 42."]]
svg.title: Polyploidy in wheat
svg.desc: The origin of bread wheat: diploid AA and BB grasses hybridise, the sterile AB hybrid doubles to tetraploid emmer AABB, which hybridises with DD goat grass, and the sterile ABD hybrid doubles to hexaploid bread wheat AABBDD.
svg.text: Polyploidy and the origin of bread wheat
Each coloured bar is one set of 7 chromosomes (x = 7). Dates approximate: about 0.5 million and 10 000 years ago.

g.data-info: Diploid: genome AA, 2n = 14 (two sets of 7 chromosomes).
A hybrid AB (2n = 14) is sterile because A and B chromosomes cannot pair in meiosis. Chromosome doubling gave AABB: tetraploid, 2n = 28, fertile.
Emmer × tauschii gave a sterile ABD hybrid (2n = 21); doubling gave AABBDD: hexaploid, 2n = 42. Polyploidy is a way new species can arise in one step (sympatric speciation).

g.text: A A B B D D
